name: first trimester bleeding overview
title: Bleeding in early pregnancy: transvaginal ultrasound read against beta-hCG sorts it into miscarriage (threatened, inevitable, incomplete, complete, missed), molar pregnancy, pregnancy of unknown location or ectopic; each column gives presentation, ultrasound and hCG findings, pathology and treatment

root.title: Bleeding in early pregnancy: is the pregnancy IN the uterus, and is it VIABLE?
lines: the 'baby' causes: spontaneous abortion · ectopic · gestational trophoblastic disease · every other cause of bleeding: see the ABNORMAL BLEEDING chart

work up every one (transvaginal first; transabdominal adds free fluid or a mass high in the pelvis): vitals · complete blood count (CBC) · group and screen (blood type, Rh D, antibodies) · quantitative beta human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) · transvaginal ultrasound of uterus + adnexa
Rh NEGATIVE + positive β-hCG + vaginal bleeding → Rh immunoglobulin (WinRho, Rhogam) to protect future pregnancies
send ALL tissue passed or sampled to pathology: only the microscope proves where the gestation was

groups.title: Intrauterine pregnancy seen: SPONTANEOUS ABORTION (miscarriage)
lines: non-viable intrauterine pregnancy (IUP) < 20 weeks · 80% before 12 weeks
bleeding, cramping, clot or tissue passed · the CERVIX and the FETAL HEART tell the types apart
~a yolk sac inside the gestational sac confirms an intrauterine pregnancy

groups.title: MOLAR PREGNANCY
lines: gestational trophoblastic disease: abnormal trophoblast proliferation

groups.title: NO intrauterine pregnancy seen
lines: abdominal pain + bleeding + positive β-hCG = ECTOPIC until proven otherwise
intrauterine device (IUD) + positive pregnancy test = ECTOPIC until proven otherwise

head: h
Threatened abortion
bleeding · cervix CLOSED
fetal heart PRESENT
20–25% of all pregnancies
path: If it continues: more risk of
preterm birth at 28–31 wk 3×, at 32–36 wk 50% higher
intrauterine growth restriction, preterm premature rupture of membranes, abruption, perinatal death
placenta previa, antepartum hemorrhage, manual removal of placenta, cesarean section

head: h
Inevitable · incomplete · complete
bleeding · cervix OPEN
tissue seen or felt through the os
pres: products partly passed, the rest in the cervix
< 10 wk fetus and placenta pass together; separately after
inv: incomplete: shows the retained products of conception
path: products of conception: chorionic villi, trophoblast ± fetal parts
must SEE products of conception to prove an intrauterine gestation
tx: Incomplete: remove tissue at the os
then expectant (91% complete by 4 wk), medical or surgical
sepsis, acute respiratory distress syndrome, acute kidney injury, disseminated intravascular coagulation, death
deaths: Clostridium sordellii, C. perfringens, group A streptococcus (toxic shock)

head: h
Missed abortion
cervix CLOSED · NO fetal heart
non-viable pregnancy retained
inv: mean sac diameter ≥ 25 mm, no embryo
no embryo with heartbeat ≥ 2 wk after a sac WITHOUT a yolk sac, or ≥ 11 days after one WITH
mean sac diameter 16–24 mm, no embryo
no embryo with heartbeat 7–13 days after a sac without a yolk sac, or 7–10 days after one with
no embryo ≥ 6 wk after the last menstrual period
yolk sac > 7 mm · sac small for the embryo (< 5 mm between mean sac diameter and CRL)
path: same findings as passed tissue (blue column)
tx: doses and success rates: see the management panel

head: h
Hydatidiform mole
COMPLETE (commonest) vs PARTIAL
inv: caught early (8–12 wk) on routine ultrasound
focal cystic change WITH a fetus
path: DIPLOID 46 XX or XY, PATERNAL only: empty ovum + 1 sperm that duplicates (90%) or 2 sperm (10%)
abundant swollen hydropic villi, NO fetal tissue · trophoblast proliferation
TRIPLOID 69 XXX or XXY: 2 paternal + 1 maternal sets; ovum + 2 sperm (diandric) mostly, or 1 that duplicates
less tissue · TWO villous sizes (hydropic + small normal or fibrotic) · irregular villi with stromal inclusions · less proliferation · fetus may be present
tx: Curettage, then serial β-hCG to baseline
complete: 80% cured · 15% invade or persist · 2–3% choriocarcinoma
partial: most cured · 5–10% invade or persist · choriocarcinoma rare
malignant trophoblast, NO villi, hemorrhage + necrosis: red hemorrhagic uterine mass
after a mole 50%, spontaneous abortion 25%, normal pregnancy 25%; even years later
bleeding + persistent, markedly ↑ hCG · diagnosis often presumptive
> 90% LUNG metastases at diagnosis; brain, liver less often
chemotherapy: 80% 5-year survival · deaths from liver or brain metastases

head: h
Pregnancy of unknown location (PUL)
positive β-hCG, NO pregnancy on ultrasound
viable IUP, non-viable IUP or ectopic
pres: varies: fading pregnancy symptoms, ongoing ones, or an ectopic's
inv: levels overlap in viable, non-viable and ectopic
β-hCG above which a sac SHOULD be seen
Normal rise in a viable IUP
≥ 53% in 2 days (99% confidence interval: < 1% slower, as low as 35%)
path: 2000–3000: ectopic 19× a viable IUP (2% chance viable)
heavy bleeding with tissue? complete miscarriage, β-hCG falling
no bleeding → high suspicion of ECTOPIC
tx: β-hCG ± ultrasound in a few days
→ non-viable IUP: falling β-hCG + no IUP = non-viable
Minimum fall in a failing IUP / 48 h
8% of untreated ectopics fall just as fast
off the curve → re-evaluate: incomplete abortion or non-resolving ectopic
β-hCG does NOT predict rupture: a falling ectopic can still rupture (0.03% of PUL, 1.7% of ectopics)

head: h
Ectopic pregnancy
implanted anywhere but the endometrium
2% of pregnancies · leading cause of early pregnancy death
pres: uterus displaced or enlarged · pelvic mass · bulging fornix · cervical motion tenderness
shoulder-tip pain (diaphragm) · rectal pain · nausea, breast tenderness
inv: β-hCG over the zone + NO intrauterine sac
adnexal mass · 'ring of fire' (blood flow around a complex mass)
yolk sac or heartbeat in the adnexa
A normal rise does NOT exclude ectopic
60% of ectopics rising at diagnosis, 21% by ≥ 53%
path: fallopian tube 80–96% (ampulla 70%, isthmus 12%, fimbria 6%) · interstitial 2% · ovary 0.5–3% · cervix < 0.1% · abdomen, cesarean scar
villi, trophoblast, fetal parts at the site
endometrium decidualized but NO products of conception
pathology: pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) commonest · adhesions (surgery, appendicitis) · endometriosis · IUD · previous ectopic
HIGH: previous ectopic or tubal surgery · tubal pathology · sterilization · IUD (past, current, levonorgestrel) · in vitro fertilization
MODERATE: previous sexually transmitted infection or PID · in utero diethylstilbestrol · smoking · pelvic or abdominal surgery
LOW: infertility · age > 40 · first intercourse < 18 · appendectomy
~an IUD itself does not raise the risk
tx: β-hCG falling AND ≤ 200 · mass < 3.5 cm · no rupture or hemoperitoneum · no symptoms · no fetal heart
reliable patient near surgical care · prefers it
STABLE · UNRUPTURED (no free fluid) · high suspicion · will follow up
before: CBC, liver enzymes (AST, ALT), creatinine, group and screen, quantitative β-hCG, transvaginal ultrasound
single dose 50 mg/m² intramuscular day 1: needs a 15% β-hCG fall day 4 → 7, else repeat
multidose 1 mg/kg days 1, 3, 5, 7 until a 15% fall

ABSOLUTE: β-hCG > 5000 · intrauterine pregnancy · breastfeeding · immunodeficiency · liver disease, alcoholism · blood dyscrasia · hypersensitivity · active lung disease (tuberculosis) · peptic ulcer · liver, kidney or blood dysfunction
RELATIVE: sac > 3.5 cm (in-class: mass > 4 cm) · embryonic heartbeat
β-hCG best predicts failure: < 5000 92% success, > 5000 4× failure
15–20% need a 2nd dose · can still rupture
gastrointestinal upset, stomatitis, ↑ liver enzymes, alopecia, pneumonitis, marrow suppression → neutropenia
UNSTABLE · rupture, impending or ongoing · previous ectopic in that tube · methotrexate contraindicated · tubal disease · can't follow up, or preference
in-class adds: β-hCG > 5000 · fetal heartbeat · significant pain
laparoscopy: 1/1000 bowel, bladder, vessel injury · ~1 week recovery · CO₂ → shoulder-tip pain

panels.title: Managing a miscarriage (inevitable, incomplete, missed)
items: EXPECTANT, up to 13+6: 4 weeks is safe, most complete by 2 · success 76% missed, 91% incomplete
mifepristone 200 mg by mouth, then misoprostol 800 mcg vaginally: expulsion 84–93%, 8.8% need D&C · in Canada approved for therapeutic abortion only · $$$

misoprostol (prostaglandin E1) alone: 800 mcg vaginally, or 600–800 mcg under the tongue or vaginally, up to 3 doses ≥ 3 h apart: expulsion 67–76%, 23.5% need D&C · THE ONE INDICATED for miscarriage in Canada · $
both: same side effects (bleeding, nausea, diarrhea, fever, pain) · no prophylactic antibiotics
SURGICAL, D&C ± suction: 95–100% successful · serious morbidity 1% · consider doxycycline 100 mg by mouth every 12 h × 2

panels.title: Why miscarriages happen
items: ABNORMAL karyotype ~50% (the #1 known cause): trisomy 16 commonest, always lethal (also 13, 18, 21, 22) · XO the commonest isolated aneuploidy · parental Robertsonian translocation → repeated losses

NORMAL karyotype 45–55%, maternal: infection (uncommon: chlamydia, mycoplasma, ureaplasma, HIV, syphilis, bacterial vaginosis, TORCH: toxoplasmosis, other, rubella, cytomegalovirus, herpes) · chronic disease (tuberculosis, carcinomatosis, celiac) · hypothyroid (severe iodine deficiency), type 1 diabetes · rarely nutrition
smoking, caffeine > 5 cups/day, alcohol, radiation > 5 rads, chemotherapy, IUD, arsenic, lead, formaldehyde, benzene · inherited thrombophilia
uterine: fibroids, adhesions (Asherman), septum, unicornuate, polyps · trauma minimal · oophorectomy < 10 wk → progesterone to 10 wk
incompetent cervix (cervical trauma, abnormal development) → cerclage: elective 12–16 wk, rescue < 23 wk

panels.title: Words and pointers
items: VIABLE: could result in a live birth · NON-VIABLE: cannot (failing IUP or ectopic)
INDETERMINATE VIABILITY: IUP not yet meeting viability criteria · PUL: positive test, nothing seen

β-hCG: made by the syncytiotrophoblast · positive 21–22 days after the last period (8 after ovulation) · serum negative < 5 · urine positive ~10 days after conception · ~100 at the missed period, ~1000 at 6 wk, peaks ~100,000 at 10 wk
when the sac, yolk sac and heartbeat should appear, and dating: see the ULTRASOUND THROUGH PREGNANCY chart
